reason: Checked against src/render.6502 2082-2151 and the listing. X = rows_m1 is kept by TAX after the STA; the byte loop touches only A and Y, so on the hot path (BCC to the test, Y = 7) CPX #8 / BCS cell does the old generic test exactly: rows_m1 >= 8 goes on through cell (TYA/SEC/SBC, which do not depend on the incoming flags), otherwise part_byte with X = rows_m1, as LDX did. The INC path falls into last_cell (LDX rows_m1, Y = 7) and the same test, which is correct for either outcome. From the cell's BCS, rows_m1 <= Y <= 7, so CPX #8 always falls through. rows_m1's final value is the same as before on every path (it is only stored where the old code stored it). AND #&3F is redundant: s_ptr+1 comes from record byte 10, which only draw_column writes (line 1743, from b_ptr's ring address &40-&7F), and A after SBC #2 is &3D-&7D, where ORA #&40 alone gives the same result; draw_column's own next cell (line 1801) uses ORA alone. Carry is unchanged (C = 0 into SBC #&7F from cell's SBC; C = 1 after SBC #2). BRA columns at &9E87 to &9E1A is in range and does not cross a page (3 cycles, the same as JMP). Byte count: +1 TAX, +4 CPX/BCS, -2 AND, -2 BRA cell, -1 JMP->BRA = 0, so nothing moves and no free space is needed. This is bank 4 renderer code with no new memory accesses (only X), no raster timing, no generated source and no protected line; on exit X = &FF and the caller saves X (PHX/PLX). Cycles: hot last cell -9, AND -2 for each next cell, +2 TAX for each first cell that is not the last, +5 for each middle cell that goes on, +4 when the first cell is also the last; a typical two-cell column saves about 9.
